title: How to forget a key
rule: An instruction sheet: numbered steps and arrowed diagrams teach the reader to forget a key.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: an instruction sheet on the LoC 1934 sheet (its grain softened by a 0.6 px blur to hold the file-size target), all in the shared pen hand (pen99 / penlib.letter_lines, penlib.brush_line): title HOW TO FORGET A KEY, 'Instruction sheet / Randolph station office / one person', 'Time required: 5 minutes (4:10 - 4:15) / No tools', a ruled head
YOU WILL NEED: six drawn parts with counts (1 x memo with its canon text, pencil, wall clock at 4:10, stranger at the ticket window, cupboard, brass key with its SERVICE tag)

six numbered boxed steps, each an imperative in the pen hand with the four canon lines verbatim, each with an arrowed line diagram: pen outlines traced from the b1m2 control-point agent, stranger, desk, window, clock, cupboard and SERVICE door (visible part of each piece, z-ordered), the key's outline from the ANRC 1922 key silhouette (99-ways-template cutout)

diagram devices: curved path arrows, a dashed floor path cut by a stop bar, a dashed eye-line to the clock, a magnifier callout on the key and its SERVICE tag, two red 'do not' signs (taking the key; opening the door) in a second pen
a result line: 'the key stays on its hook; the SERVICE door stays shut'; folio '32 / How to forget a key' (pen99.folio)

events.E0: step 1: read the memo (canon text), get up, set off for the cupboard; diagram desk -> arrow -> cupboard
events.E1: step 2: let a stranger at the ticket window stop you + the question; diagram: path interrupted, arrow from window
events.E2: step 3: look up at the clock (4:10), answer + the answer; diagram: eye-line to the clock at 4:10
events.E3: step 4: accept her thanks + 'Much obliged!', let her go, walk on; diagram: she turns to the platform
events.E4: step 5: open the cupboard, look at the key on its hook (tag SERVICE); diagram: open cupboard, LOOK arrow, magnifier
events.E5: step 6: pencil to chin, ask the forgetting line, leave the key; diagram: '?', key on hook, SERVICE door shut, two do-not signs; result line

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the sheet is written step by step: head and parts list, then each numbered step and its diagram, ending with the do-not signs and the result line
beat_frames: b07: + step 6 and the result line (E5) = the page

self_check.check: A reader finds numbered imperative steps (1-6 in circled numbers, each an imperative) with arrowed diagrams (maker's judgement from the full-size page; blind reading pending)
